note: Both sets contain the same 25 facts from the furniture and millwork schedules, and every dimension string, quantity and tag binding checks out against the page; neither set has a misread, misbound or invented claim. Set A names rows with their descriptions (e.g. BASE CABINET (SINK) MWK04, TALL CABINET (MWD01)) while Set B uses bare tags, but both bind values to the correct rows. The two sets share the same gaps: most quantity values, the F10 patio side table row, and the entire equipment, plumbing and finish schedules are absent, and both support the F5 quantity claim with a quote ("2") that does not identify the row.
remarks: Both extractions cover only the furniture and millwork schedules plus one QZ thickness; the equipment, plumbing and finish schedules (manufacturers, models, tile sizes, colours, glass thickness, wall base profile) are entirely missing from both, as are most QUANTITY values (F2, F3, F7, F8, F9, F10 and all millwork quantities) and the F10 PATIO SIDE TABLE (S/2) row. The text layer is column-scrambled (tags printed after dimension strings, all quantities dumped in one block, the MWK01 description 'BASE CABINET' displaced to the end of the millwork block), which is the likely cause of the row-binding difficulty; the page image resolves the alignment. The F5 quantity claim in both sets uses a quote ('2') that cannot be tied to the row without positional context.
